rationale: Pass 10 reconciled the one corpus number the `imports` verdict never had to reconcile: `css-ontology-probe.ts` counts 250 `import_statement` NODES on the admitted corpus and production `parseFile` published 243 `imports` EDGES. `processImport` read only a DIRECT `string_value` / `call_expression` child, and 7 statements the pinned CSS grammar recovers into an ERROR shape carry the quoted specifier as a `string_value` node one level down — `;+@import+ERROR+binary_expression`, `;+@import+ERROR+ERROR+float_value+keyword_query` and five siblings, all of them `.sass` partials under `Documenter.jl/assets/html/scss/bulma/`. `@import "../utilities/mixins"` is a real fetch, so publishing nothing was a silent 7-edge miss on a type already reported EMITTED, which is the coverage-asserted-but-not-measured failure the `extends` row committed in pass 6. The fix is `findImportNameNode`: direct child first (so the 243 already published are untouched), then the first `string_value` / `call_expression` at ANY depth whose row equals the `@import` KEYWORD's own row. The line guard is the load-bearing half and this file is what pins it. ERROR recovery SWALLOWS the rest of the file into the `import_statement` node — the corpus file `bulma/elements/button.sass` spans L2..L50 and carries ELEVEN `string_value` descendants, one at L2 (the module) and ten at L47 (a `$breakpoints` map's "mobile", "small", "normal", ...). The `$map: ( "a-key": 1, "b-key": 2, )` block below reproduces that inside one small file: `"a-key"` and `"b-key"` are real `string_value` nodes on L16 and L17, INSIDE the `import_statement` node that spans L13..L19. A descendant search without the row guard would publish `"a-key"` as a module the stylesheet never imports. `forbidRelationships` refuses both, so the guard is asserted and not merely implemented. The Sass placeholder syntax and the `$map` block are in a `.css` file for one reason: they are what this grammar cannot parse, which is the only way to reach the branch. A well-formed stylesheet never gets there, and the third statement (`@import url("theme.css")`) is the control that proves the direct-child path still fires alongside it. CONTRACT REPIN (2026-10-25): `part_of` is now emitted for the PLAIN FILE FORM of `@import` in the css family — exactly one named child of type `string_value`, no `.css` suffix, no protocol URL, no `sass:`/`data:` scheme. Sass/Less fold that form in at compile time, so it is a source inclusion (`part_of`, `partRole:"library"`), not a stylesheet load. Every other form keeps `imports`: `url(...)` (the child is a call_expression), a media query (a SECOND named child), a `.css` specifier, and any protocol URL. This is a LABEL MOVE — source, target, line and the project-file claim are unchanged.
knownLimitation: The published module name is the specifier exactly as written, so a relative import keeps its `../` (`../utilities/mixins`) and does not resolve against the importing file's directory. That is unchanged from the 243 edges published before this fix and is why this lane's `imports` both-ends resolution rate is 0% rather than a defect count — see the `imports` row of the six-questions table. The line guard reads the `@import` KEYWORD node's row; for a statement whose keyword and specifier are split across lines by the multi-line `url(...)` form, the direct-child rule still fires first, so this fixture does not claim the recovered path handles that form.
